title: Multilingual Probing of the Same Concept Direction

original_idea.body:
# Multilingual Probing of the Same Concept Direction

**Problem:** Whether a concept direction extracted in English fires for the same concept in other languages is rarely directly probed.

**Direction:** Extract a difference-of-means direction for a simple concept in English on a multilingual open model. Test it on translated prompts in 3-4 languages; measure probe accuracy degradation per layer.

**Why it matters:** Safety monitors trained in English may be blind in other languages, a known but under-measured gap.

**Relevant context:** Refusal transfers between English and Chinese; difference-of-means probing standard.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: English-built safety monitors being blind in other languages is a concrete global-deployment safety gap.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Difference-of-means + translated prompts; guided, mentor helpful for multilingual data quality.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped: probe accuracy degradation across 3-4 languages per layer.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Under-measured multilingual probe-generalization labs deprioritize; public models.

novelty.reasoning: Cross-lingual concept representations studied somewhat; a clean per-layer probe-transfer study may be partly open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Cross-lingual concept representations studied somewhat; a clean per-layer probe-transfer study may be partly open.
